hook: The $7.92 layer most bedroom makeovers skip

scenes.visual_prompt: Extreme close-up of a foam panel tile edge, showing a slightly stiff, geometric corner line
scenes.on_screen_text: Foam panels have a hard edge
scenes.voiceover: However nice the fabric, a foam-core panel has a stiff, geometric edge up close.

scenes.visual_prompt: Reference shot of a hotel room with a sheer fabric layer visible behind heavier drapery
scenes.on_screen_text: Hotels soften that edge with sheers
scenes.voiceover: Hotel rooms break that line with a layer of sheer fabric between the drapery and the wall.

scenes.visual_prompt: Product graphic of white sheer curtain panels with overlay showing 4.7 stars, 17,073 reviews, $7.92
scenes.voiceover: This sheer set is $7.92 for the pair — the cheapest single thing in this whole setup.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands hanging sheer curtains on a second inner rod closer to the wall, layered behind a blackout panel
scenes.on_screen_text: Inner rod, closer to the wall
scenes.voiceover: Hang it on a second rod closer to the wall, behind the blackout panel, and it breaks up where the tiles meet bare drywall.

scenes.visual_prompt: Before and after of the panel wall with and without the sheer layer visible
scenes.on_screen_text: This is the detail that gets skipped
scenes.voiceover: It's under eight dollars and it's the most commonly missing piece in before-and-afters that don't quite land.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final wide shot of the bedroom with soft diffused daylight through the sheer layer
scenes.voiceover: Cheapest line item. Easiest one to forget.

caption: This is the eight-dollar layer I keep seeing missing from panel-wall makeovers that almost land but don't. Full writeup on the blog.
